Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

run a javascript command in wkwebview swift","url":"https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/63333411/how-do-i-run-a-javascript-command-in-wkwebview-swift"},{"title":"sending message to wkwebview throws error","url":"https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/58166604/sending-message-to-wkwebview-throws-error"}]

The search didn't turn up a direct answer, but the results point to a clear pattern. An exception thrown inside code run through `evaluateJavaScript` comes back to Swift as an error, and `window.onerror` is a separate path.

- **Errors from `evaluateJavaScript` arrive as NSErrors.** Developers see WKErrorDomain code 4 with a "JavaScript exception occurred" description, and the error details include the JS message and line number when available. Example: Error Domain=WKErrorDomain Code=4 "A JavaScript exception occurred" appears in one thread. Check the completion handler or the async `throws` version for these.
- **`window.onerror` is for uncaught errors in page scripts.** A WebKit bug report says unhandled JavaScript exceptions call the user's window.onerror function if there is a function installed. The sources don't say whether an exception from an `evaluateJavaScript` call itself fires it. My understanding is that it doesn't, so the error comes back to the caller instead.
- **On WKWebView, the details are often censored.** The same bug report says unhandled JavaScript exceptions doesn't generate useful information to window.onerror beyond msg = "Script error". A later Apple Developer Forums thread reports the same problem, with same results, still censored.
- **Common workaround:** Have the `onerror` handler forward the message, URL, line, and column to Swift through `window.webkit.messageHandlers`. One Stack Overflow answer does this, and the forum poster's handler does too.

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Nov 15 21:30:10 2026 -0800

    Report unexpected errors to the JusPrin team, and fix four bugs found on the way
    
    When something fails that no person can act on, JusPrin now shows one
    dialog, "Something went wrong on our side" (boards agent-ui-11 to 16),
    instead of a sentence about that particular failure. The person can see
    the whole report, press "Report to JusPrin team", or tick "From now on,
    report errors like this automatically". The report goes to JusPrin's
    server (/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports), which passes it to Sentry.
    
    Why: under the error-handling rules, a failure with no outcome a person
    decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry point and is
    reported there, instead of each site writing its own sentence. Kenneth
    agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this approach."
    
    The reporting path
    - Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
      sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
      dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its dialog
      waits is queued once; after the person answers, the next occurrence
      opens the dialog again, and every occurrence is sent when reports are
      automatic (Kenneth: "leave it"). A report holds the app and OS versions,
      what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
      home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
      and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
      token or cookie.
    - Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens. Its
      line "no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or
      email address" stays although other error text can quote a file name
      (Kenneth: "Keep the promise and accept the risk.").
    - Top handlers: the AI pages' and Home's message handlers, the file
      picker's callback (it reads the chosen files after the page's message
      was handled), and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
      "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
      until the page has connected).
    - An exception that leaves any other native event is handled exactly as
      OrcaSlicer handles it; no OrcaSlicer-owned file is changed. Kenneth: "it
      should behave the same as the upstream. no reason to use a diff
      behavior here for the fork".
    - Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box, "Report errors to the
      JusPrin team automatically", off by default.
    
    Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
    - "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
    - "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a

    - "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)

content.text:
I found five problems in the two pages, plus one I couldn't confirm. The worst is that a page error in the first moments after the page loads reaches nobody. Everything below was checked by reading only; I ran no code.

The pages' top error handler lives in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/WebShared/`, outside the two folders you named. I audited it because the page errors reach the app only through it.

**Findings, most serious first**

1. **A page error before the bridge client starts is never reported.** `WebShared/bridgeClient.ts:104` starts Sentry's handlers inside `client.start()`. That runs from a `useEffect` (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx:149-150`, `HomeUI/src/App.tsx:67-68`, and the other `*App.tsx` files), which fires only after the first render. Before it, `i18n.tsx:62` activates the language on import, and modules build translated text at their top level (`credits.ts` `TIER_NAMES`, `SIGNUP_OFFER`; `history.ts` `REPORT_OFFER`). An error there or in the first render has no handler. With React 18 and no error boundary, the person sees a blank AI panel or a blank Home, and no "Something went wrong on our side". Sentry gets nothing. This breaks "one handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure".

2. **Errors waiting for the handshake are thrown away if it never finishes.** `bridgeClient.ts:155` holds a report until connected, and only `hello_ack` (line 180) sends it. If the state ends at `timeout`, `no-transport` or `incompatible`, the reports are lost. That is when one may explain why the page failed to connect. The person sees the older "The AI chat didn't start…" pane, and Sentry gets nothing.

3. **A print report that fails unexpectedly can end with no word to the person.** In `HomeUI/src/components/PrintReportForm.tsx:51-55,138`, the `'unexpected'` state just re-enables Send, with no sentence. The page relies on the app's dialog, but `Support/ErrorReport.cpp:108-111` opens none when automatic reports are on. Lines 113-114 open none for a failure already answered earlier in the run. In both cases the person presses Send, sees "Sending…", then the button comes back and nothing is said. The API-key form handles the same case by showing "Something went wrong on our side" (`AgentConnection.tsx:411`).

4. **Delete account tells people to check their internet whatever went wrong.** `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:281,296` shows "The account couldn't be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try again." for every `deleted:false`.
   - In this release, the app also refuses while a printer or filament chat is replying (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2581`). That person is sent to check a network that works.
   - On the native side, `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:157` turns a server error into `false` and drops its status and body, with no report. That is outside this scope.
   - A commit in this release says this wording is "to be decided", so Kenneth has not approved it. It breaks "a sentence of its own for a failure the person can do nothing about".

5. **A missing translation catalog fails silently.** `AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx:33` (`catalog?.messages ?? {}`) gives a default value for a build bug. A listed language with no catalog renders untranslated text with no error. I did not check whether that means English or message ids. `catalogs.test.ts` guards against it at build time, so this is minor.

6. **Unconfirmed:** the app delivers messages to the pages by running script with no completion handler (`Widgets/WebView.cpp:511-527`). My guess is that an error thrown synchronously in a page's message handler goes back to that script call, not to the page's `"error"` event, so it is dropped. A web search ([Stack Overflow](https://kaweah.freedombox.rocks/kiwix/content/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/50229935/wkwebview-get-javascript-errors), [Apple forums](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/25454), [WebKit bug 147753](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=147753)) did not settle it. A test should throw inside `onEnvelope` and watch for a report.

**Older than the release, but it matters**

`AgentUI/src/App.tsx:310` and `HomeUI/src/App.tsx:217` silently swallow a file the browser cannot read. That predates this release. But a commit in this release moved the app's own equivalent ("The file could not be read.") to the report path, so the pages now go against that.

**Outcomes that look designed but have no app table entry**

The app has no expected-errors table, so these sit apart from the findings:
- "is not a complete email address" and "photo larger than 20 MB": Kenneth said "Yes, all three".
- "That photo could not be read.": it is in the server's table.
